title: Does glutathione help heavy metal detox/chelation?

grade.title: No qualifying human study in this corpus
grade.basis: No qualifying human trial was located.

answerHtml: No human trial of glutathione with a metal outcome was located in this corpus. N-acetylcysteine is a different compound. A study of N-acetylcysteine and blood lead is graded C on the N-acetylcysteine page and is not evidence about glutathione. Not graded is not a finding that glutathione has no effect.

sections.heading: What was searched
sections.html: The corpus records a PubMed search that located the N-acetylcysteine worker study and did not locate a glutathione trial with a metal outcome. Kasperczyk 2013, the NAC study.

sources.text: Kasperczyk et al. 2013 (N-acetylcysteine, not glutathione), PMID 23731375

buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
